elements.element: Preferred: no non-compete or field-of-use restriction imposed on Customer (Ono)
elements.evidence: "neither Ono or its Affiliates ... shall Commercialize in the Ono Territory: (i) a product that includes ... an agent that is a [ * ]"

elements.element: Preferred: no field-of-use limitation on Customer's own commercialization
elements.evidence: "or grant the right to a licensee or distributor to Commercialize in the Ono Territory any of the above described products (each a \"Competing Product\")"

elements.element: Fallback: restriction limited to a named competing product
elements.evidence: "an agent that is a [ * ] (other than Binimetinib)" ... "\"[ * ]\" means a compound that [ * ]" — the restricted class is a redacted mechanism/compound class rather than a single named product

elements.element: Fallback: restriction operative during the term only (no post-termination tail)
elements.evidence: "then neither Ono nor its Affiliates shall Commercialize a Competing Product ... prior to the twelve (12) month anniversary of the date such termination takes effect"

elements.element: Fallback: restriction duration capped at 12 months
elements.evidence: post-termination tail now reads "the twelve (12) month anniversary", but the in-term restriction runs "Prior to the [ * ]" — its length is redacted and therefore not shown to be within 12 months

elements.element: Fallback: carve-out for Customer's internal development
elements.evidence: "This Section 8.2 shall not restrict Ono or its Affiliates from internal development"
"or from Commercializing a Competing Product acquired in a merger with, or acquisition of, a Third Party or of its business or assets"

reasons: The two carve-outs required by the fallback (internal development and M&A-acquired products) are now express and operative, and the post-termination tail is fixed at twelve (12) months, so the open-ended survival risk is resolved.
The fallback contemplates a restriction operative during the term only; a twelve-month post-termination restraint on Ono still survives expiry/termination, so that element is not literally met.
The in-term restriction period remains "Prior to the [ * ]" — its duration is redacted, so the 12-month cap cannot be verified for the in-term restraint; only the tail was capped.

The restricted scope is a redacted compound/mechanism class ([ * ] inhibitors other than Binimetinib/Encorafenib), which is broader and less determinate than the fallback's "named competing product"; consider narrowing to identified products if the redacted definitions prove class-wide.

Edits are surgical (one number replacement plus one concise carve-out sentence) and leave the reciprocal Array-side exclusivity and the royalty/termination mechanics intact, so minimality and intent are preserved.
